ns2:section.sectionText: Topic Section Q: Creative Non-Fiction In this course, we will read a range of autobiographical and biographical writing that can be qualified as ?creative? or ?literary? non-fiction. We will explore the texts as celebrations of life as well as interrogations of identity. We will also examine the texts as constructed narratives, or as constructed ?truth,? investigating the rhetorical strategies employed by the writers to forge their diverse identities on the page. As this is an advanced composition course with a focus on writing about literature, assignments will include three formal papers (7-9 pages) with drafts, multiple shorter response papers, and in-class writing assignments. Students will also do an oral presentation. It is strongly recommended that all English and Teaching of English majors take ENGL 300 and ENGL 301 BEFORE taking any other 300- or 400-level courses.
